questions.q: Refer to the following letter and symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. (Left) T O @ $ J $ S € M L I * N G © Y & T P £ Y T (Right) How many such symbols are there each of which is immediately preceded by a letter and also immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.solution:
Only @ meets both conditions: O is immediately before it and $ immediately after it. Count qualifying symbols, not all symbols.
**Answer: 1**

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (336, 216, 156) (379, 259, 199)
questions.solution:
Subtract 120 from the first number and 60 from the second. Only 412 → 292 → 232 uses both subtractions.
**Answer: (412, 292, 232)**

questions.q: Below are given two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Similarly, a certain mathematical operation on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the question? (NOTE – A two/three-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations. E.g. if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3+7 as a two-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits.) 157 – 162 – 172 – 86 93 – 98 – 108 – 54
questions.solution:
The operations are +5, then +10, then divide by 2. The sequence 185 → 190 → 200 → 100 fits all three.
**Answer: 185 – 190 – 200 – 100**

questions.q: A is the wife of B. B is the father of C. D is the brother of C. E is the son of D. How is A related to E?
questions.solution:
D is B’s son and A is B’s wife. E is D’s son, so A is E’s paternal grandmother: his father’s mother.
**Answer: Father's mother**

questions.q: Refer to the following letter, symbol series and answer the question. Counting to be done from left to right only. (Left) O N & # K € S * P # £ * G I & * @ I A * @ © (Right) How many such letters are there each of which is immediately preceded by a letter and also immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.solution:
The qualifying letters are N, the I after G, and A. Each has a letter immediately before it and a symbol immediately after it.
**Answer: 3**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-clusters should replace # and % so that the pattern and relationship followed between the letter-cluster pair on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of :: ? # : NMH :: VUP : %
questions.solution:
Move every letter five places backwards. SRM becomes NMH, and VUP becomes QPK.
**Answer: # = SRM % = QPK**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘ROAD’ is coded as ‘9416’ and ‘DORM’ is coded as ‘3691’. What is the code for ‘M’ in the given code language?
questions.solution:
The common letters R, O and D use the common codes 9, 1 and 6. The only extra letter in DORM is M, so M uses the remaining code 3.
**Answer: 3**

questions.q: If 1 is added to each odd digit and 1 is subtracted from each even digit in the number 21673458, what will be the product of the greatest and smallest digit in the new number thus formed?
questions.solution:
The transformed digits are 1, 2, 5, 8, 4, 3, 6, 7. Greatest × smallest = 8 × 1 = 8.
**Answer: 8**

questions.q: In a certain code language, A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’, A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’, A + B means ‘A is the wife of B’ and A % B means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is E related to B if ‘E % R # D + N @ B’?
questions.solution:
N is B’s son and D is N’s wife. R is D’s sister, and E is R’s father. Thus E is the father of B’s son’s wife.
**Answer: Son's wife's father**

questions.q: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 64 62 59 54 47 ?
questions.solution:
The differences are -2, -3, -5, -7, the successive prime numbers. The next subtraction is 11, giving 47 - 11 = 36.
**Answer: 36**

questions.q: In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements is sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer. A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. Who sits to the immediate right of C? (I) D sits to the immediate left of F. C is the immediate neighbour of A and E. (II) B sits second to the left of F. C sits second to the right of F.
options: Both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question.
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not.
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.
Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question.
questions.solution:
Even with both statements, A and E can exchange the two neighbour positions around C. That changes C’s immediate right neighbour, so the answer is not uniquely determined.
**Answer: Both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question.**

questions.q: Each of P, Q, R, S, T, U and V has an exam on a different day of a week starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. Only two people have exams before Q. Only three people have exams after V. Only three people have exams between S and Q. P has the exam immediately before T but not on Monday. R does not have the exam on Tuesday. How many people have exams between R and T?
questions.solution:
The days from Monday to Sunday are R, U, Q, V, P, T, S. R is on Monday and T on Saturday, leaving four people between them.
**Answer: Four**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘WAND’ is coded as ‘1846’ and ‘GNAW’ is coded as ‘4165’. What is the code for ‘G’ in that language?
questions.solution:
W, A and N occur in both words and correspond to 1, 4 and 6. G occurs only in GNAW, so its code is the remaining digit 5.
**Answer: 5**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-clusters should replace # and % so that the pattern and relationship followed between the letter-cluster pair on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of :: ? # : NQW :: LOU : %
questions.solution:
Each letter advances six places, with wraparound after Z. HKQ becomes NQW and LOU becomes RUA.
**Answer: # = HKQ, % = RUA**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some ants are lizards. All lizards are spiders. No spider is a rat. Conclusions: (I) Some rats are lizards. (II) Some spiders are ants.
questions.solution:
Some ants are lizards and every lizard is a spider, so some spiders are ants. No lizard can be a rat because no spider is a rat. Only conclusion II follows.
**Answer: Only conclusion (II) follows**

questions.q: Seven people B, C, D, O, P, Q and R are sitting around a circular table facing the center of the table. P sits third to the left of Q. Only one person sits between Q and B when counted from the right of Q. Only two people sit between O and C when counted from the left of O. D is an immediate neighbor of O. Who sits third to the right of R?
questions.solution:
Fix Q and place P three positions to its left and B two to its right. The O–C spacing and D next to O fill the remaining places, with R in the final gap. The person third right of R is P.
**Answer: P**

questions.q: The product of two numbers, X and Y, is 6760, and the HCF of X and Y is 13. Find the number of possible pairs (X,Y), given that X>Y.
questions.solution:
Write X = 13a and Y = 13b with coprime a and b. Then ab = 6760/169 = 40. The coprime pairs with a > b are (40, 1) and (8, 5), giving two pairs.
**Answer: 2**

questions.q: Manan starts from Point A and drives 42 km towards South. He then takes a left turn, drives 40 km, turns left and drives 54 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 48 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 12 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
questions.solution:
North–south movement cancels: -42 + 54 - 12 = 0. East–west movement is 40 - 48 = -8 km. He ends 8 km west of A, so must drive 8 km east to return.
**Answer: 8 km to the east**

questions.q: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 19 20 28 55 119 ?
questions.solution:
Add the consecutive cubes 1³, 2³, 3³ and 4³. Next add 5³ = 125 to 119, giving 244.
**Answer: 244**

questions.q: TN 13 is related to WR 16 in a certain way. In the same way, KE 18 is related to NI 21. To which of the following is VP 26 related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Advance the first letter three places, the second four places, and the number by three. VP 26 therefore becomes YT 29.
**Answer: YT 29**

questions.q: Seven boxes A, B, C, D, E, F and G are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept below A. Only two boxes are kept between E and A. F is kept immediately above B. D is kept above G but below A. How many boxes are kept below C but above B?
questions.solution:
From top to bottom the order is C, E, F, B, A, D, G. E and F lie below C and above B, giving two boxes.
**Answer: Two**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? PMO 51 SPR 46 VSU 41 YVX 36 ?
questions.solution:
Each letter advances three places in every term, while the number decreases by five. After YVX 36 comes BYA 31.
**Answer: BYA 31**

questions.q: This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below. (Left) 194 582 419 149 825 (Right) (Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7) What will be the resultant if the third digit of the highest number is added to the second digit of the lowest number?
questions.solution:
The highest number is 825, whose third digit is 5. The lowest is 149, whose second digit is 4. Their sum is 9.
**Answer: 9**

questions.q: If 1 is added to each odd digit and 2 is subtracted from each even digit in the number 4813576, what will be the difference between the highest and the lowest digits in the number thus formed?
questions.solution:
The new digits are 2, 6, 2, 4, 6, 8, 4. Highest - lowest = 8 - 2 = 6.
**Answer: 6**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? EGE 85 DFD 90 CEC 95 BDB 100 ?
questions.solution:
Every letter moves one place backwards while the number increases by five. BDB 100 is followed by ACA 105.
**Answer: ACA 105**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All oranges are apples. No apple is a banana. No banana is a kiwi. Conclusions: (I) No orange is a banana. (II) No apple is a kiwi.
questions.solution:
All oranges lie inside apples, and apples exclude bananas, so no orange is a banana. Apples and kiwis may overlap; their relation is not fixed. Only conclusion I follows.
**Answer: Only conclusion (I) follows**

questions.q: Below are given two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Similarly, a certain mathematical operation on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the question? (NOTE – A two/three-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations. E.g. if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3+7 as a two-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits.) 15 – 225 – 235 – 195 9 – 81 – 91 – 51
questions.solution:
Square the first number, add 10, then subtract 40. The matching sequence is 18 → 324 → 334 → 294.
**Answer: 18 – 324 – 334 – 294**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster)
questions.solution:
Three pairs shift both letters forward by three. In BD → EH, B advances three but D advances four, so this pair is different.
**Answer: BD-EH**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster)
questions.solution:
The usual shift is +3 for both letters. In DF → GJ, D moves +3 but F moves +4, making it the odd pair.
**Answer: DF-GJ**

questions.q: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. D sits to the immediate right of A. Only three people sit between D and G when counted from the left of D. Only three people sit between A and F when counted from the right of F. E sits to the immediate right of B. How many people sit between D and E when counted from the right of D?
questions.solution:
Place D immediately right of A and then use the D–G and F–A gaps. The remaining adjacent B–E pair fixes E’s place. Four people lie between D and E when counted from D’s right.
**Answer: 4**
